head_commit.message:
fix(schemas): accept the canonicalization labels the verifier accepts

Six published schemas pinned `canonicalization` to the legacy constant
"RFC8785-JCS", while the kernel mints every new artefact with
ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1 (CANONICALIZATION_PROFILE) and its verifier accepts
both (ACCEPTED_CANONICALIZATION_PROFILES). Every freshly minted PCCB,
receipt/refusal correlation digest, approval, countersignature and
transparency digest therefore failed the kernel's own schema.

The schemas now allow exactly the accepted set. A new test walks every
schema and asserts each canonicalization constraint equals the
verifier's accepted profiles, so a schema can drift from the verifier
in neither direction.

head_commit.message:
fix(cli): verify-receipt/refusal stop saying "verified" for unchecked artifacts; verify-proof --public-key-jwk (F10)

`verify-receipt --receipt X` printed "Receipt verified." after only
parsing X: a v1 Receipt carries no signature, and with no linked
artifact nothing is compared, so a fabricated or tampered receipt
"verified" (E2E F10). Same for verify-refusal.

Now:
- with no linked artifact the command exits 1 with "Receipt NOT
  verified: only its structure was checked"; --structure-only makes a
  shape check explicit and still says NOT verified.
- with links it prints "Receipt links verified.", what it was checked
  against, verifies the linked PCCB's signature when a verifier is
  available (local key or --public-key-jwk) and fails if it does not
  verify, and states that the receipt itself is unsigned (pointing at
  the attestation commands).

`verify-proof` only knew the public local HMAC key, so Ed25519 proofs
(what actenon-permit mints) failed with "no local verifier". New
--public-key-jwk verifies against an explicit issuer JWK through the
same hardened path as well-known discovery (kid and alg must match the
proof; raw 32-byte Ed25519; RSA >= 2048), fully offline.

test_cli_happy_paths asserts the new "... links verified." wording.

head_commit.message:
fix(outcomes): resolve compatibility aliases before disclosure mapping (F11)

to_disclosed_code()/to_retryable() handed kernel codes straight to the
protocol's catalogue lookups, which only know canonical codes. The
codes the kernel actually emits for replay, expiry, revocation, missing
proof, and parameter/intent mismatch (DUPLICATE_REPLAY, PCCB_REQUIRED,
PCCB_EXPIRED/EXPIRED, REVOKED, ACTION_HASH_MISMATCH, INTENT_MISMATCH)
are catalogue compatibility aliases, so they disclosed OUTCOME_UNKNOWN
with retryable=True — telling a caller to retry a replayed proof.

Aliases are now resolved with actenon_protocol.resolve_alias() first
(e.g. DUPLICATE_REPLAY -> REPLAY_DETECTED, retryable=False). Unknown
codes still fall back to OUTCOME_UNKNOWN per the catalogue's forward-
compatibility rule. to_internal_code() is unchanged (trusted callers
keep the granular kernel code).

head_commit.message:
fix(outcomes): resolve compatibility aliases before disclosure mapping (F11)

to_disclosed_code()/to_retryable() handed kernel codes straight to the
protocol's catalogue lookups, which only know canonical codes. The
codes the kernel actually emits for replay, expiry, revocation, missing
proof, and parameter/intent mismatch (DUPLICATE_REPLAY, PCCB_REQUIRED,
PCCB_EXPIRED/EXPIRED, REVOKED, ACTION_HASH_MISMATCH, INTENT_MISMATCH)
are catalogue compatibility aliases, so they disclosed OUTCOME_UNKNOWN
with retryable=True — telling a caller to retry a replayed proof.

Aliases are now resolved with actenon_protocol.resolve_alias() first
(e.g. DUPLICATE_REPLAY -> REPLAY_DETECTED, retryable=False). Unknown
codes still fall back to OUTCOME_UNKNOWN per the catalogue's forward-
compatibility rule. to_internal_code() is unchanged (trusted callers
keep the granular kernel code).

head_commit.message:
docs(mcp): add a verified Claude Code one-liner and pin launch commands

The MCP docs only gave a JSON config block, so Claude Code users had to
translate it into `claude mcp add` by hand. The natural translation,
`uvx actenon-kernel --from actenon-kernel[mcp] actenon-mcp --demo`, fails:
uvx reads its own options only before the command name, so it runs the
`actenon-kernel` CLI (without the [mcp] extra) and hands it the rest as
arguments. Claude Code reports "Failed to connect - CONNECTION_CLOSED".
Unquoted, the extra also aborts in zsh with "no matches found".

- README and MCP_QUICKSTART: add
  `claude mcp add actenon -- uvx --from 'actenon-kernel[mcp]' actenon-mcp --demo`,
  verified with `claude mcp list` / `claude mcp get` reporting Connected.
- MCP_QUICKSTART: explain the two hand-writing pitfalls (--from order,
  quoting) and `--scope user`.
- Test: pin every mcpServers JSON block and every `claude mcp add` line in
  both docs to one argv, and require the extra to be quoted. Mutation-
  checked: the misordered command, an unquoted extra, misordered JSON
  args and a removed one-liner each fail it.
